justifications.c1: No sourced cost for a housing-PTP blower failure incident; the only per-incident money is a replacement blower at ~£309–371 (retailer, attribution inferred), and the Anglian Water £156k case is water-company scale and not comparable.
justifications.c2: No blower failure rate found; servicing is annual or six-monthly, with quarterly in some landlord contracts (Eastlight, attribution inferred), and the sensor does not replace that servicing.
justifications.c3: Paid multi-site servicing and desludging contracts are documented with values (Stonewater £780k est., search-confirmed; Connexus £120k; Eastlight ~£90k/yr), but the sensor would not remove them, and the blower-failure workaround is resident complaints or local alarms.
justifications.c4: The file itself shows the 2014 EPR amendment removed registration and 5-year maintenance-record duties (search-confirmed via IEMA and the consultation), alarms are 'not a legal requirement', and no EA enforcement against a housing association PTP was found; GBRs only say 'don't pollute'.
justifications.c5: Housing associations buy through formal tenders with named budgets, but no job title or budget holder is evidenced and the route is public procurement.
justifications.c6: Service contractors (CSG, Premier Tech, Bates, Mayglothling) visit on a cycle and Premier Tech runs 24/7 call-out for a national housing association, but none is shown selling or bundling remote monitoring.
justifications.c7: Commoditised: on-site blower low-pressure alarms (Envirosure 100), GSM blower alarms (ASIO AS-GSM, Bonnel Sequetrol, Barnett Protalk), and Cotterill SmartServ Pro £564; the claimed fleet-dashboard gap is inferred from absence, and the £41.95 Envirosure price was mismatched (it is the beacon's price).
justifications.c8: Pressure-switch blower-fail detection is established and mains power is on site, but no prices for the proposed NB-IoT/LTE-M build were searched, rural mobile coverage is flagged as a precondition (ASIO), and plant warranties may restrict fitting; the cited £41.95 component price is mismatched.
justifications.c9: No statutory record-keeping duty since 2014 (the file's own key finding), so recurring value rests only on existing service contracts; no comparable subscription pricing.
justifications.c10: One Housing Ombudsman case (Onward Homes, content on blower failure not shown), a Paignton holiday-park EA case via a fishing site, and two Irish local-news items; no trade press or regulator data on housing PTP failures.

weakest: Compliance hook removed: since 2014, English small-sewage-discharge operators need not keep maintenance records, and cheap blower-failure and GSM alarms already exist, so there is neither a records duty nor an evidenced gap to fill.
